messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED — High 5xx rate on serving-runtime cluster us-west-2 (autoscaler flapping). Alert ID: INC-20260315-87. See: https://infra.redwood/alerts/INC-20260315-87

mike (eng-oncall): ack, paging in. I’m on call — pulling logs now.

anya: taking lead for runtime. @mike can you paste the error samples?

mike (eng-oncall): copying a few lines from pod logs:
```
E 2026-03-15T02:24:12.345Z serving: cuda runtime error: out of memory
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/runtime/worker.py", line 212, in handle_request
    model.forward(input)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 128.00 MiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total; 30.12 GiB already allocated; 64.00 MiB free; 29.87 GiB reserved)
```
multiple pods show the same OOM followed by container restart backoff.

leo (eng-sre): I’m seeing scale events coincident with the OOMs — HPA and our custom autoscaler are both reacting. It looks like rapid scale ups then immediate scale downs (thrash). When nodes come up, several pods schedule and try to prime KV caches which pushes memory above threshold -> OOM -> crashloop -> autoscaler interprets as low readiness and scales down.

raj (infra): Confirmed node flaps too — new GPU nodes failing health checks after boot: 
```
[2026-03-15T02:24:09Z] kubelet: container runtime setup: nvml init failed: CUDA_error: 3
[2026-03-15T02:24:10Z] node-manager: node marked NotReady: kernel module missing
```
Looks like the AMI in the recent autoscaler image build had an incompatible NVIDIA kernel module.

kate (support): Support reports ~22 customers seeing 503s and timeouts to embed/generate endpoints since 02:23 UTC. Top affected customers: acct-143, acct-920, acct-774. Escalating to account reps.

mike (eng-oncall): immediate mitigation ideas: 1) pause autoscaler so we stop thrashing 2) cordon new node pool to avoid scheduling on potentially bad AMI 3) scale down gracefully to a stable capacity we know works

anya: agreed. I’ll pause autoscaler and pin to current replica count. Executing now.

anya: /runbook autoscaler pause -> `autoscaler.lock create INC-20260315-87`

deploy-bot: autoscaler.lock created by anya (reason: emergency pause for scale thrash).

leo (eng-sre): cordoning nodepool gpu-autoscale-usw2-2026-03-15
```
kubectl cordon node gpu-autoscale-usw2-03a
kubectl drain node gpu-autoscale-usw2-03a --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```
Node cordoned, workloads rescheduled to stable nodes.

raj (infra): rolling back the autoscaler AMI rollout to last known-good (ami-7f9b3d) and disabling the new image.

support-bot: Customer-facing incidents: posting status update to status.redwood.com — message: "Investigating increased error rates for serving API in us-west-2; mitigation in progress. No data loss."

kate (support): sending targeted emails to top affected customers, linking to status page.

mike (eng-oncall): After pause + cordon: we're seeing reduced crashloops but still leftover OOMs from pods that primed large caches. I suggest clearing KV cache priming for in-flight startups — add config flag `--no-prime-cache` for rolling restart to avoid memory spike.

anya: good call. Will set `NO_CACHE_PRIME=1` in runtime env for a canary deployment on stable nodes.

leo (eng-sre): rolling restart command: 
```
kubectl set env deploy/runtime-runtime NO_CACHE_PRIME=1 -n runtime-prod
kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime-runtime -n runtime-prod --selector=pool=stable
```
Canary up: one pod with NO_CACHE_PRIME is healthy. CPU/mem stable.

mike (eng-oncall): two quick checks: 1) are there any recent deploys to runtime in last 30 mins? 2) was autoscaler config changed?

deploy-bot: deploy `runtime:6b32a` rolled 2026-03-15T01:58Z by ci-cd (sha:6b32a). No config changes to autoscaler on that deploy.

raj (infra): autoscaler config rollback in progress. We should also add a temporary debounce window to avoid reacting to short-lived readiness changes. I’m applying a 120s stabilization window.

anya: applying stabilization: `autoscaler.set --stabilization-window 120s --namespace runtime-prod`

leo (eng-sre): Good — that should prevent immediate downscales while pods finish startup. Monitor for 10m.

support-bot: support tickets updated: 22 customers flagged, 7 high-impact, CS reps alerted.

kate (support): sharing a canned message to CS: "We're mitigating increased error rates due to autoscaler/node image mismatch causing OOMs. We paused scaling and rolled back the AMI; services are recovering. ETA 30-60min."

mike (eng-oncall): monitoring metrics: 5xx rate dropped from 14% -> 4% after pause + cordon + canary restart. Latency still elevated for some requests.

leo (eng-sre): Observed node boot logs show NV driver mismatch for the new AMI. We'll blacklist that AMI and add preflight check to autoscaler pipeline.

raj (infra): blacklisted AMI and forcing nodes with ami-7f9b3d to be used for scaling.

anya: starting controlled scale up of stable pool to restore capacity: `kubectl scale deploy/runtime-runtime --replicas=12 -n runtime-prod`

mike (eng-oncall): scaling up; watching memory per pod. If any pod shows OOM pattern, mark for recycle and do not let autoscaler react.

leo (eng-sre): After stable scale up, 5xx now ~1.2% and dropping. No new OOMs.

kate (support): sending update to customers: "Services recovering; continuing to monitor. Apologies for the disruption."

anya: plan for next steps: 1) postmortem, 2) add AMI preflight GPU driver checks in CI, 3) add autoscaler stabilization default 2m, 4) mitigation playbook update (pause + cordon pattern).

mike (eng-oncall): assigning owners: raj -> AMI preflight; leo -> autoscaler stabilization defaults; anya -> playbook update; kate -> customer comms/postmortem liaison.

deploy-bot: Incident state changed to: mitigated (operator: anya). Closing pager.

mike (eng-oncall): great work team. I’ll kick off an incident postmortem doc and include logs/graphs. Anyone else with important logs or notes paste here.

raj (infra): I’ll attach node boot tracelogs and AMI diffs to the postmortem.

leo (eng-sre): I’ll add the autoscaler timeline and metric graphs.

kate (support): I’ll assemble customer impact list and ticket summaries.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — mitigations in place. Root cause path: incompatible AMI + rapid autoscaler reactions -> node flaps -> pod priming memory spike -> OOMs -> crashloops -> autoscaler thrash -> customer-facing errors. Postmortem link: https://docs.redwood/incidents/INC-20260315-87/postmortem

mike (eng-oncall): last check: 5xx 0.6% over last 5m. closing thread in 30m unless new alerts. Thanks all :white_check_mark:
